dossier.architecture: Two-sided acquisition, differential-speed fixed-heading shooter and elevator amp/trap carriage.

subsystems.drivetrain: Beta Thrifty swerve; beltless module architecture.
subsystems.intake: Front and rear intake; extra leading roller reaches notes against the wall.
subsystems.transfer: Shooter normally stages the note; reverse/feed sequence redirects it into the scoring carriage.
subsystems.scoring: Independent left/right wheel speed adds flight-stabilizing spin; pivoted launcher.
subsystems.endgame: Climb supports elevator/carriage trap delivery; exact hook transmission is not explained in this walkthrough.
subsystems.controls: Three Limelights, full-field pose, selectable autonomous orders; note tracking used selectively.

versions: Added differential wheel speeds after long-range notes dived. Added wall-acquisition roller. At Champs, favored faster odometry-based acquisition over slower note tracking in some autos.
dossier.analysis: Explicit turret alternative: dual-sided pickup can recover much of the cleanup-cycle benefit with a simpler transfer. Sensors are chosen by time-to-complete, not by their availability.
limits: Only source-established configurations and changes are described; intermediate revisions may remain unresolved.

context_documents.title: 2024-1706 · Two acquisition directions were the alternative to a turret
context_documents.body:
# 2024-1706: Two acquisition directions were the alternative to a turret

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The robot has front/rear acquisition, an extended leading roller for wall notes, and a pivoted differential-speed launcher. Reversing the staged note redirects it to the amp/trap carriage. Its swerve uses selectable gearing, with a middle setting in the filmed configuration.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly says turret complexity would burden the intake and handoff, so it chose two intakes instead. It reports fast local cleanup as a benefit; the brief amplified-period claim is a team account, not a universal four-note cycle benchmark.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Directional independence can be purchased at the collector instead of the launcher. This can reduce turning during pickup while retaining simpler aiming hardware, but adds a second collision face and more transfer states. The correct comparison is total useful scoring under the expected note distribution and defense, including reversal into the amp carriage.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare opposite-direction acquisition cycles with a one-intake baseline, and test handoff after a note enters off-center from either side.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/C-kz6RLoH24](https://youtu.be/C-kz6RLoH24)

source_reviews.title: Ratchet Rockers Riot CAD release and replies
facts: Elevator belts were mechanically unlinked and required turnbuckle adjustment. The team describes a belt-clamped carriage that reaches the stops of successive stages and pushes them up.
Elevator was controlled with a trapezoidal profile and elevator feedforward. Hood used proportional control at the time of the post and had experienced gear skipping.
Late changes included a steel shaft at the hood and an offseason elevator motor change. The published code omits the trap command.
source_reviews.limitations: The team describes final CAD as approximate. The wording about diametral pitch is not enough to reconstruct the gear specification.

source_reviews.title: Ratchet Rockers Riot reveal
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team announcement and climb reply
facts: The team used the Thrifty climber kit because fabrication time was limited.

source_reviews.title: Riot Behind the Bumpers
facts: Dossier describes front/rear intake, staged note reversal to a scoring carriage, pivoted launcher and lateral wheel speed differences.
source_reviews.limitations: Full captions not reviewed in this pass.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Riot gave drivers two directions from which to capture a note. The inherited description puts the speaker shooter at the normal staging point and uses reverse feed to move the note toward the amp/trap carriage. The team's CAD replies show how the late-added elevator and hood survived different problems. The elevator needed both belt sides aligned throughout travel, while the hood needed a stiffer shaft and revised mesh to address tooth skipping.
piece_flow: Front or rear pickup brings the note into a common internal path, according to the inherited study.
The usual route stages the note for a speaker shot. A reverse sequence redirects it to the elevated scorer.
The operator climbed, then manually commanded maximum elevator height in the trap method described by the team.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The energy chain feeds power and CAN to the carriage. Include its bend envelope with the note in transit and while each stage bottoms or extends. An unsynchronized pair of belts can work when guide friction and belt lengths are balanced. Stiffening the top structure does little if the drives can gain or lose a tooth relative to one another.

subsystems.name: Dual pickup and transfer
subsystems.construction: Inherited front/rear capture and reverse transfer into carriage.
subsystems.operation: Choose the accessible approach and reverse for alternate scoring.
subsystems.team_rationale: No new statement of pickup rationale beyond the inherited study.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Two entrances can save a chassis turn if the shared path reliably handles either direction. A second mouth can also leave a note stranded at an inactive roller or create simultaneous-entry risk.
subsystems.interfaces: Common staging point and reverse path must remain defined for either entry.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Proposed tests include both directions with off-center notes and reversing a partly staged note.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact sensor placement and feed code.

subsystems.name: Belt elevator
subsystems.construction: Two belt sides, adjusted with turnbuckles. Carriage clamps to belt, and later stages follow as preceding travel stops are reached.
subsystems.operation: Use a profiled elevator command for carriage movement. The trap routine held full extension after climb.
subsystems.team_rationale: Team reported difficulty preventing rack and tooth skip and would change the unlinked arrangement.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Travel stops create concentrated loads if the motor keeps pushing. Compare synchronized and independent sides using loaded asymmetry, settling and stall current.
subsystems.interfaces: Carriage guides, belt phase, stop geometry, energy chain and lift-to-scorer timing.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: The team reports an offseason pulley/encoder-wire incident. Inspect side travel equality and pulley temperature before a repeated full-extension test.
subsystems.unknowns: Load, thermal limits, actual interlocks and detailed stage geometry.

subsystems.name: Shooter pivot and climb
subsystems.construction: Team reports toothed hood motion and a steel shaft revision. Thrifty climb is confirmed separately.
subsystems.operation: Aim the launcher and engage the chain using a separately packaged kit.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team noted a swinging center of mass and proposed gravity compensation. Kit selection saved manufacturing time.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A gravity model can improve settling, but tooth mesh under shock is a separate mechanical requirement. Evaluate backlash under torque reversal and frame twist.
subsystems.interfaces: Hood pinion shaft support and chain hook clearance with elevator raised.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Look for skip and angle loss under controlled impact. Verify repeat calibration after shaft replacement.
subsystems.unknowns: Gear specification, shaft spans and event mapping.

revisions: Amp/trap elevator installed just before Central Missouri. Hood transmission changed midseason. Published CAD contains changes following an offseason elevator incident.
transferable_principles: Require alignment checks and a recovery path for each parallel elevator drive. Separate control tuning from gear-mesh durability.
disconfirming_conditions: Dual pickup loses its advantage if a shared handoff introduces frequent recoveries. Unlinked belts are a poor transfer when frequent asymmetric loading prevents stable carriage alignment.
remaining_gaps: Review of public source beyond release replies, full captions and as-built CAD-to-event mapping.
